title: Kitlet quicklaunch paths and fallthroughs (draft)
content:
TL;DR: Kitlet is a tiny opinionated SDK starter (single-file, CLI-first) to get a real prototype calling Redwood in under 5 minutes. This note sketches three lowest-friction paths, fallback rules when things break, required telemetry hooks for product metrics, and a minimal gating checklist for shipping as a supported quickstart in the console.

Context and goal:
- Problem: customers hit friction in first 15 minutes: env/keys, tokenization surprises, streaming hookup, and lack of small examples that map to production patterns.
- Kitlet intent: extremely small surface area: one install, one config file, one command to run a sample app that demonstrates text generation, streaming, and an embeddings call.
- Audience: full-stack engineers (fast demo), data scientists (explore embeddings), infra/platform teams (validate private deployment connectivity).

Paths (three personas):
1) Full-stack engineer (fastlaunch)
  - preconditions: node 18+, yarn or npm, Redwood API key copied to env.
  - commands (happy path):
      npm i -g @redwood/kitlet || yarn global add @redwood/kitlet
      export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
      kitlet init --template=todo-demo
      cd todo-demo && kitlet run --stream
  - expected output: local web page at http://localhost:3000 with streaming completions and a small token cost indicator.
  - fallthroughs: missing API key -> kitlet prints an interactive helper to open the console or paste the key; network blocked -> kitlet switches to a small local LLM shim with a notice (non-prod).

2) Data scientist (embed-first)
  - preconditions: python 3.10, pip, ability to write files.
  - commands:
      pip install redwood-kitlet-py
      REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_abc python -c "from kitlet import Embeds; print(Embeds(['doc a','doc b']).cosine_matrix())"
  - expected: cosine similarity matrix + small CSV export sample.
  - fallthroughs: rate limit -> kitlet suggests smaller batch sizes and a cache file; local env without GPU -> use hosted embeddings with cost estimate.

3) Platform engineer (private-connect)
  - preconditions: VPC peering allowed, KMS key id if using customer-managed key.
  - commands:
      kitlet configure --mode=private --proxy=http://10.0.0.5:3128
      kitlet smoke-test --route=/v1/generate --concurrency=10
  - expected: a short report with 95th percentile latency and a model fallback log showing behavior if a requested variant is unavailable.
  - fallthroughs: TLS handshake issue -> kitlet prints cert troubleshooting steps and a single command to dump debug traces for SRE.

Cheat-sheet: small checks to run when onboarding customers
- verify API key scope: kitlet whoami
- quick rate/quotas: kitlet quotas --project=default
- streaming smoke: kitlet stream-check --example=chat
- embedding cache size: kitlet cache-stats

Minimal reproducible example (file: kitlet.demo.js):
  - a 12-line example that shows request, streaming callback, and telemetry event. (We keep the snippet inside the kitlet package for copy/paste.)

Telemetry and product signals (required):
- install events: kitlet.install -> counts by platform (npm/pip).
- quickstart completion: kitlet.onboard_complete (goal: 40% within 10m).
- common errors: kitlet.error.{missing_key,rate_limit,network_block} with a free-text short hash for grouping.
- feature used signals: kitlet.feature.{streaming,embeddings,private-connect}.
- opt-in debug logs: kitlet dbg --collect -> uploads a single anonymized tarball (customer consents).

Gating checklist to add this quickstart to Console surface (proposed):
- [ ] single-command start works on Mac/Linux/Win (WSL)
- [ ] docs page with three persona flows and screenshots
- [ ] CI smoke tests for kitlet run that use a controlled sandbox key
- [ ] telemetry events wired to product analytics (production schema)
- [ ] fallback shim documented and gated as non-prod (must clearly label)
- [ ] accessibility: web demo basic a11y checks

UX fallthrough rules (how kitlet chooses fallback path):
1) If API key missing -> interactive helper -> if user chooses not to paste, offer a sandbox demo (local shim).
2) If network blocked to Redwood endpoint -> detect corporate proxy, attempt to respect proxy env vars, else switch to cached-model shim and surface: "non-production demo mode".
3) If streaming fails mid-session -> switch to polling mode and continue with a short notice banner (includes last-known-token index so UI can continue).
4) If embeddings batch fails with 413/limit -> auto-split and retry up to 3 shards. Report aggregate latency and costs.

Open questions / risky decisions:
- Do we bake the shim LLM into the installer or download on demand? (tradeoff: bundle size vs offline reliability).
- How aggressive should kitlet be in emitting product telemetry by default? (opt-out vs opt-in).
- Naming and discoverability in Console: "Quickstart" vs "Kitlet demo" vs "Sample SDK".

Next steps (short):
- prototype the node kitlet CLI and the python minimal package (2 wk small spike). Owner: Marcus.
- design telemetry schema and an internal dashboard bubble for onboard completion (Aisha owns analytics).
- run a 1-week hackathon to get 10 internal teams to hit the 5-minute goal and collect failure traces (Dana organizes).

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- Week 1: spike + internal demo.
- Week 2: add streaming + embed path.
- Week 3: private connect checks + telemetry.
- Week 4: polish docs + smoke CI + ship as "beta quickstart" in Console.

Contact: Marcus Chen (marcus@redwood.ai) — ping for pairing on the CLI prototype.

This is intentionally scrappy — meant to be a living working doc for the kitlet quicklaunch effort.
